name: Billie Morrow
life: “My first senior route was two dinners and one very heavy holiday cake.” Sunday often includes a stop at Tideline Market, where Billie picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I returned the ring inside a soup tin to keep it dry. Nobody checked the empty containers.
appearance: Billie has a center part and straight chestnut hair, heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a striped cotton shirt. It usually goes with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. When somebody else has the floor, Billie gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Billie has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To tell the route leader where the dry soup tin went.
family: Eden Diaz is Billie’s second cousin. Billie offers the first invitation. Eden gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The rescue hut mural*, Eden says, “I always thought she was diving. From my wheelchair she's clearly reaching for somebody.”
connections: Marc Ramos. The soup tin has to travel another route with a rider who now knows where it belongs.

reactions.situation: A tenant refuses to hand back a spare key
reactions.response: Billie asks the tenant what access they would be giving up.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Billie lets the child choose whether to stand by the door or sit beside the window while another adult gets help.

reactions.response: Billie asks for the name of the person who will still be around tomorrow.
